title: ICH 112 - Industrial Reaction and Separation Technology

items.q: A process could give 200 kg of product but actually yields 160 kg. Find the percentage yield.
items.s: Yield = (actual ÷ theoretical) × 100 = (160 ÷ 200) × 100 = 80 per cent.

items.q: A reaction produces 100 kg of the wanted product together with 20 kg of an unwanted by product. Find the mass of by product formed per 100 kg of wanted product.
items.s: By product per 100 kg of product = (20 ÷ 100) × 100 = 20 kg.

items.q: A reaction has a product of molar mass 140 and the reactants together have a molar mass of 160. Find the atom economy.
items.s: Atom economy = (molar mass of product ÷ total molar mass of reactants) × 100 = (140 ÷ 160) × 100 = 87.5 per cent.

items.q: A solution has a hydrogen ion concentration of 10 to the power minus 4 mol per litre. Find its pH.
items.s: pH = minus log of the hydrogen ion concentration = 4.

items.q: A solution has a pH of 6. Find its hydrogen ion concentration in mol per litre.
items.s: Concentration = 10 to the power minus pH = 10 to the power minus 6 = 0.000001 mol per litre.

items.q: A solution has a pOH of 5 at 25 degrees celsius. Find its pH.
items.s: pH + pOH = 14, so pH = 14 − 5 = 9.

items.q: 50 ml of a 0.5 molar acid is titrated against a 0.5 molar base. Find the volume of base needed at the end point.
items.s: Ca Va = Cb Vb, so Vb = (0.5 × 50) ÷ 0.5 = 50 ml.

items.q: At equilibrium the liquid mole fraction of the lighter component is 0.2 and the vapour mole fraction is 0.7. Find the relative volatility.
items.s: Relative volatility = [y ÷ (1 − y)] ÷ [x ÷ (1 − x)] = 9.33.

items.q: A fertiliser has a molar mass of 80 and each formula unit contains 3 nitrogen atoms. Find the percentage of nitrogen by mass.
items.s: Mass of nitrogen per mole = 3 × 14 = 42 g. Percentage = (42 ÷ 80) × 100 = 52.5 per cent.

items.q: 5 kg of a fuel of calorific value 55000 kJ per kg is burned completely. Find the heat released in megajoules.
items.s: Heat = mass × calorific value = 5 × 55000 = 275000 kJ, which is 275 MJ.

items.q: The total heat of formation of the products of a reaction is -1200 kJ per mol and that of the reactants is -750 kJ per mol. Find the heat of reaction.
items.s: Heat of reaction = products − reactants = (-1200) − (-750) = -450 kJ per mol.

items.s: BOD = (initial − final) × dilution factor = (8 − 1.5) × 2.5 = 16.25 mg per litre.

items.q: environmental impact assessment may be defined as
o: the rearrangement of hydrocarbon molecules to improve their quality
the reduction of waste at source rather than its treatment afterwards
the study of the likely effects of a plant before it is approved
the instruction given to a newcomer on the hazards and rules of a plant
items.s: environmental impact assessment: the study of the likely effects of a plant before it is approved. The other options describe safety induction, reforming, waste minimisation.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines azeotrope.
o: a mixture that distils at constant composition
the share of the product stream that is the wanted substance
a reaction that absorbs heat
a substance added in small amount to improve catalyst performance
items.s: azeotrope: a mixture that distils at constant composition. The other options describe endothermic reaction, purity of a product, promoter.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines batch reaction time?
o: the degree to which a catalyst favours the wanted product
the processing of liquid waste before discharge
the period for which a batch is held at reaction conditions
the release of fine solid particles in a gas stream
items.s: batch reaction time: the period for which a batch is held at reaction conditions. The other options describe particulate emission, effluent treatment, selectivity of a catalyst.

items.q: Which of the following best describes reforming?
o: the written instruction for carrying out a task the same way each time
a reaction that proceeds in a single step as written
the vessel in which separation by volatility is carried out
the rearrangement of hydrocarbon molecules to improve their quality
items.s: reforming: the rearrangement of hydrocarbon molecules to improve their quality. The other options describe distillation column, standard operating procedure, elementary reaction.

items.q: Which term is described by “a mixture that distils at constant composition”?
o: crystallisation
purity of a product
leaching
azeotrope
items.s: azeotrope is a mixture that distils at constant composition.

items.q: The statement “the equipment that removes particles from a gas by electrostatic attraction” describes which of the following?
o: permissible limit
scrubber
precipitator
chemical oxygen demand
items.s: precipitator is the equipment that removes particles from a gas by electrostatic attraction.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines tablet granulation.

the reduction of waste at source rather than its treatment afterwards

items.s: tablet granulation: the preparation of powder particles so that tablets form properly. The other options describe catalyst, waste minimisation, order of reaction.

the release of fine solid particles in a gas stream
the conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into a combined form
the nitrogen fertiliser made from ammonia and carbon dioxide
items.s: industrial attachment: the supervised period of work in industry required of a student. The other options describe particulate emission, nitrogen fixation, urea.
